added_lemmas.statement:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the three signed measures
\[
 \gamma_v^\pm=\lambda_v^\pm-3p_0^\dagger,
 \qquad \gamma_d^\pm=\lambda_d^\pm-2p_0^\dagger,
 \qquad \gamma_0=\delta_{111}-\delta_{000}
\]
have total mass zero and respective centered marginal moments \(\pm v\), \(\pm d^\dagger\), and \(\mathbf1\).  Their target first moments are \(\pm1\), \(0\), and \(0\), and their target second moments are \(5/8\), \(3/16\), and \(0\).  The law in \(\mathrm{def:explicit\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}airy\text{-}tube}\) is therefore a probability distribution whenever \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\leq1\), and it satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E[b_t\mid x,h,\zeta]
 =\alpha_n(xv+hd^\dagger+\zeta\mathbf1),
 \quad
 \mathbb E[\theta_t\mid x,h,\zeta]=\alpha_nx,
 \quad
 \mathbb E[\theta_t^2\mid x,h,\zeta]
 =\alpha_n\left\{\frac58|x|+\frac3{16}|h|\right\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
For the three two-arm faces \(F=\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\}\), respectively, the paths
\[
 (h_F(x),\zeta_F(x))
 =\left(\frac43x,-\frac12x\right),
 \quad
 (-4x,-\tfrac12x),
 \quad
 (0,\tfrac12x)
 \tag{2}
\]
have target derivative one and zero marginal derivative on every arm in \(F\).  Each single-arm face is contained in one of these faces.  The corresponding positive and negative signed response-type directions have target-second-moment costs \(7/8\), \(11/8\), and \(5/8\).  For every \(|x|\leq1\), all six paths give probability laws once \(\alpha_n\leq1/10\); hence the face-guard width is fixed, rather than vanishing with \(n\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The exact-primitives proposition gives
\[
 \sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^\pm=3,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^\pm b_t=\pm v,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^\pm\theta_t=\pm1,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{v,t}^\pm\theta_t^2=\frac58,
 \tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 \sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^\pm=2,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^\pm b_t=\pm d^\dagger,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^\pm\theta_t=0,
 \quad \sum_t\lambda_{d,t}^\pm\theta_t^2=\frac3{16}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Both atoms of \(p_0^\dagger\) have \(\theta_t=0\), while
\(\sum_tp_{0,t}^\dagger b_t=0\).  Also
\[
 \sum_t(\delta_{111}-\delta_{000})(t)b_t
 =b_{111}-b_{000}=\mathbf1,
 \qquad
 \theta_{111}=\theta_{000}=0,
 \tag{5}
\]
where the last equality uses \(\sum_ac_a^\dagger=0\).  Subtracting the indicated multiples of \(p_0^\dagger\) in (3)--(5) proves every mass, marginal, target-first-moment, and target-second-moment assertion about \(\gamma_v^\pm,\gamma_d^\pm,\gamma_0\).  Substitution in the construction then proves (1).

It remains to check positivity and the faces.  Away from the types \(000\) and \(111\), the perturbation is a sum of nonnegative multiples of the displayed \(\lambda\)'s.  At either central type its negative part is bounded by
\[
 \alpha_n\left(\frac32|x|+|h|+|\zeta|\right)
 \leq\frac12
\]
under \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\leq1\).  Since the central mass is \(1/2\), all eight coordinates are nonnegative; the zero-total-mass identities make their sum one.  This proves exact positivity.

For a pair \(F\), write
\(z_F(x)=xv+h_F(x)d^\dagger+\zeta_F(x)\mathbf1\).  Direct substitution of
\[
 v=(1/2,-1/2,-1/2),
 \qquad d^\dagger=(0,3/4,-1/4)
\]
gives
\[
 z_{\{1,2\}}(x)=(0,0,-4x/3),
 \quad
 z_{\{1,3\}}(x)=(0,-4x,0),
 \quad
 z_{\{2,3\}}(x)=(x,0,0).
 \tag{6}
\]
Thus the observed marginal slopes on the indicated face are zero.  Moreover
\((c^\dagger)^\top z_F(x)=x\), either from (6) or from
\((c^\dagger)^\top v=1\),
\((c^\dagger)^\top d^\dagger=0\), and
\((c^\dagger)^\top\mathbf1=0\).  Hence every path has target derivative one.  Combining the second moments in (3)--(5), its cost per unit \(|x|\) is
\[
 \frac58+\frac43\frac3{16}=\frac78,
 \qquad
 \frac58+4\frac3{16}=\frac{11}{8},
 \qquad
 \frac58,
 \tag{7}
\]
respectively.  Finally, direct inspection of the two central coordinates of each of the six signed directions shows that their largest negative coefficient in absolute value is at most five; all noncentral coefficients are nonnegative.  Therefore \(p_0^\dagger+\alpha_n|x|\Gamma_F^{\operatorname{sign}(x)}\) is nonnegative for \(|x|\leq1\) whenever \(5\alpha_n\leq1/2\).  This is \(\alpha_n\leq1/10\), and proves the fixed-width assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(n,k\geq1\) and rational \(\varepsilon>0\) for which the scalar subprior is admissible,
\[
 G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(n,0,0)
 \geq \frac{11}{8}\int_{\mathbb R}|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
\frac{45}{256}\varepsilon.
\]
Consequently, if \(k_n\to\infty\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n}^{\dagger,\mathrm A,0}(n,0,0)
 \geq\frac{22}{15}\Lambda_{c^\dagger}>
 \Lambda_{c^\dagger}.
\]
Thus the scalar subprior cannot furnish the zero-face part of a sharp all-count converse; the added common-shift coordinate is load-bearing.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Under allocation \((n,0,0)\), set
\(\widetilde\tau_n=n^{-1}\sum_i(2Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1)\) and
\(e(t)=2t_1-1-(c^\dagger)^\top t\).  The exact target identity gives
\(\widetilde\tau_n-\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)=n^{-1}\sum_ie(t_i)\).  In lexicographic type order,
\[
 e(t)^2=(1,1/16,9/16,0,0,9/16,1/16,1).
\]
The scalar construction and the explicit response measures give
\[
 \mathbb E[e(t)\mid x,h]=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[e(t)^2\mid x,h]
 =1-\alpha_n\left(\frac{11}{8}|x|+\frac9{16}|h|\right).
\]
Conditional independence therefore makes the risk of \(\widetilde\tau_n\)
\[
 \frac1n-n^{-4/3}\left\{
 \frac{11}{8}\int|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
\frac9{16}\int|h|\rho_\varepsilon(h)\,dh\right\}.
\]
Direct integration yields
\(\int|h|\rho_\varepsilon(h)\,dh=5\varepsilon/16\).  Since the posterior mean has no larger Bayes risk, rearrangement proves the first inequality.

For \(\Phi=\phi_{c^\dagger}\), scaling
\(\Phi_s(x)=s^{1/2}\Phi(sx)\) in the Airy Rayleigh quotient and differentiating at its minimum \(s=1\) gives
\[
 \int|x|\Phi(x)^2\,dx
 =\frac{2\Lambda_{c^\dagger}}{3\kappa(c^\dagger)}
 =\frac{16}{15}\Lambda_{c^\dagger}.
\]
The weighted \(H^1\) convergence in the effective normalized Airy-record lemma and normalization of \(w_k^\dagger\) imply
\(\int|x|w_k^\dagger\to16\Lambda_{c^\dagger}/15\).  Discarding the nonnegative transverse term gives the stated lower limit.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\leq1\).  Under the face-robust permutation-invariant prior \(\nu_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\), every outcome-independent assignment law and every possibly randomized labeled-data estimator have Bayes risk at least
\[
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)
 \mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
 \geq B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
\]
Conditional on a fixed allocation count, the posterior mean of the exact finite-population contrast attains the displayed fixed-count Bayes risk.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The tangent lemma proves that the stated admissibility condition makes every fiber an eight-type probability law.  Mixing the multinomial count vector and then choosing a labeling uniformly in its orbit is equivalent, conditional on \((x,h,\zeta)\), to drawing the labeled response types independently from that fiber: for a labeled sequence with count vector \(m\), the multinomial coefficient and reciprocal orbit size cancel.  Integration over the three coordinates preserves invariance under a common permutation of the unit labels.

Fix an outcome-independent assignment law.  The prior is independent of that law by construction.  Conditional on a realized assignment vector with count \(r\), exchangeability of the prior permits a common unit permutation carrying the assignment to the canonical fixed-count assignment without changing the joint law of the response types or the exact target
\(n^{-1}\sum_tm_t(c^\dagger)^\top t\).  Hence the conditional observation kernel is the factorial likelihood in \(\mathrm{def:three\text{-}arm\text{-}orbit\text{-}likelihood}\).  For squared loss, completion of the square gives, for every action \(d\),
\[
 \mathbb E[(d-\tau)^2\mid r,x^{\mathrm{obs}}]
 =\operatorname{Var}(\tau\mid r,x^{\mathrm{obs}})
 +\{d-\mathbb E(\tau\mid r,x^{\mathrm{obs}})\}^2.
\]
Thus estimator randomization cannot improve upon the posterior mean, and summing the posterior variances over \(x^{\mathrm{obs}}\) gives exactly
\(\mathcal B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\).  Averaging over the induced count law \(\pi\) gives the first displayed bound, and averaging numbers each at least their minimum gives the second.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(k\geq1\) and rational \(\varepsilon>0\), and define
\[
 \mathcal E_{k,\varepsilon}
 =\frac{4\int_{\mathbb R}|(\varphi_k^\dagger)'|^2
 +(5/8)\int_{\mathbb R}|x|(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}
 {\int_{\mathbb R}(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}
 +\frac{15}{256}\varepsilon.
\]
For every rational \(\eta>0\), a terminating rational calculation returns an integer \(N(k,\varepsilon,\eta)\) such that, whenever \(n\geq N(k,\varepsilon,\eta)\),
\[
 \alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\leq1,
 \qquad
 \max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
 G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
 \leq\mathcal E_{k,\varepsilon}+\eta.
 \tag{8}
\]
Moreover, if \(r_n/n=q^\dagger+n^{-1/6}u_n\), \(\mathbf1^\top u_n=0\), and \(u_n\to u\), then
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r_n)
 \leq\mathcal E_{k,\varepsilon}
 -2\sum_{a=1}^3\frac{u_a^2}{|c_a^\dagger|}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus the local design saddle is at \(q^\dagger\); after \(k\to\infty\) and then \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), its coefficient is \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\).  The calculation covers positive exterior counts and every zero-count face, and its threshold is effective from the verified rational spline record.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(\alpha=n^{-1/3}\), \(q=r/n\), and
\[
 H(q)=\frac14\sum_{a=1}^3\frac{(c_a^\dagger)^2}{q_a}
 \tag{10}
\]
when every \(q_a>0\).  Since \(q_a^\dagger=|c_a^\dagger|/2\), Cauchy--Schwarz and direct expansion give the exact identities
\[
 H(q)\geq1,
 \qquad
 H(q)-1=\sum_{a=1}^3\frac{(q_a-q_a^\dagger)^2}{q_a}.
 \tag{11}
\]
Conditional on the prior coordinates, the cancellation of multinomial and orbit factors in the orbit lemma shows that the labeled response types are independent.  A unit observed in arm \(a\) is Bernoulli with mean
\[
 p_a(z)=\frac12+\alpha z_a,
 \qquad z=xv+hd^\dagger+\zeta\mathbf1,                 \tag{12}
\]
by (1).  Let \(P=\alpha x\) and let
\(H_n=n^{-1}\sum_i\theta_{t_i}\), which is the exact finite-population target.  No prior mean is substituted for \(H_n\).

We first lower-bound the Bayes risk for \(P\).  For positive \(q\), put
\[
 d_a(q)=\frac{c_a^\dagger}{4q_aH(q)}.
 \tag{13}
\]
Then \((c^\dagger)^\top d(q)=1\) and
\[
 \sum_aq_ad_a(q)^2=\frac1{4H(q)},
 \qquad
 |d_a(q)|\leq|c_a^\dagger|^{-1}.                       \tag{14}
\]
The three vectors \(v,d^\dagger,\mathbf1\) form a basis, so uniquely
\(d(q)=v+\beta(q)d^\dagger+\gamma(q)\mathbf1\).  The coefficient of \(v\) is one because the other two basis vectors are orthogonal to \(c^\dagger\).  If \(I_k=4\int| (\varphi_k^\dagger)'|^2/\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2\), the directional Fisher information of the product prior density is exactly
\[
 J(q)=I_k+\frac{10}{\varepsilon^2}
 \{\beta(q)^2+\gamma(q)^2\}.                           \tag{15}
\]
Indeed, the three coordinate scores have mean zero, their cross products integrate to zero under the product density, the longitudinal information is \(I_k\), and direct integration of \(\rho_\varepsilon\) gives
\[
 \int_{-\varepsilon}^{\varepsilon}
 \frac{\rho_\varepsilon'(s)^2}{\rho_\varepsilon(s)},ds
 =\frac{10}{\varepsilon^2}.                            \tag{16}
\]
The bound in (14) and the fixed inverse of the displayed rational basis give a finite, explicitly rationally bounded constant \(J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max}\) with \(J(q)\leq J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max}\) for every positive \(q\).

We derive, rather than assume, the information inequality used below.  Let \(\Pi\) denote the product prior density in the coordinates \((x,h,\zeta)\), and let \(L_z(o)\) be the Bernoulli likelihood from (12).  The amplitudes generating all three factors vanish on the boundary of their compact supports.  Weak integration by parts in direction \(d(q)\), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz, gives for every estimator \(D(o)\)
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \alpha
 &=\mathbb E[(D-P)\{\partial_{d(q)}\log\Pi
                  +\partial_{d(q)}\log L_z(O)\}],\\
 \mathbb E(D-P)^2
 &\geq\frac{\alpha^2}{J(q)+I_O(q)}.
 \end{aligned}                                         \tag{17}
\]
The cross term between the prior score and the likelihood score is zero because the latter has conditional mean zero.  If the compact support of \(z\) is bounded by \(Z_{k,\varepsilon}\) in maximum norm and \(2\alpha Z_{k,\varepsilon}<1\), (12)--(14) give
\[
 I_O(q)
 =\sum_a r_a\frac{\alpha^2d_a(q)^2}
 {p_a(z)\{1-p_a(z)\}}
 \leq\frac{n\alpha^2}{H(q)}L_n,
 \quad
 L_n=\{1-4\alpha^2Z_{k,\varepsilon}^2\}^{-1}.          \tag{18}
\]
Consequently the posterior-mean Bayes risk \(B_P(q)\) for \(P\) satisfies
\[
 B_P(q)\geq
 \frac{H(q)}{n\{L_n+J(q)H(q)n^{-1/3}\}}.              \tag{19}
\]

We next transfer (19) to the realized causal target.  For positive \(q\), define the observable Horvitz--Thompson average
\[
 \overline T=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
 \frac{c_{A_i}^\dagger(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1/2)}{q_{A_i}}.
\]
Conditional on \(z\), \(\mathbb E\overline T=P\) and
\(\mathbb E(\overline T-P)^2\leq H(q)/n\).  If
\(\mu=\mathbb E(P\mid O)\), posterior orthogonality yields
\[
 S(q):=\mathbb E(\overline T-\mu)^2
 =\mathbb E(\overline T-P)^2-B_P(q)
 \leq\frac{H(q)}n
 \frac{L_n-1+J(q)H(q)n^{-1/3}}
 {L_n+J(q)H(q)n^{-1/3}}.                               \tag{20}
\]
Put \(W_n=H_n-P\) and \(\zeta_O=\mathbb E(H_n\mid O)\).  The finite response alphabet, (1), compact support, and the lower bound
\(p_a(z),1-p_a(z)\geq1/4\) imply an explicit rational constant
\(C_{k,\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
 \left|\mathbb E(\theta_t-P\mid z,A_i=a,Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=y)\right|
 \leq C_{k,\varepsilon}\alpha.                        \tag{21}
\]
One may compute the least such displayed bound by enumerating the eight types, the six arm--outcome pairs, and the finitely many sign cells.  Conditional independence and the fact that each conditional summand in (21) has mean zero give
\[
 D(q):=\mathbb E(\zeta_O-\mu)^2
 \leq C_{k,\varepsilon}^2\frac{\alpha^2}{n}.           \tag{22}
\]
The moment identities (1) give exactly
\[
 \mathbb EW_n^2
 =\frac1n\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(\theta_t\mid x,h,\zeta)
 \leq n^{-4/3}\overline V_{k,\varepsilon},
 \quad
 \overline V_{k,\varepsilon}
 =\frac58\int|x|w_k^\dagger(x)\,dx
  +\frac{15}{256}\varepsilon.                          \tag{23}
\]
The coefficient \(15/256\) uses
\(\int|h|\rho_\varepsilon(h)\,dh=5\varepsilon/16\).

There is also an exact covariance identity.  Since
\(\sum_ac_a^\dagger(t_a-1/2)=\theta_t\), independence across units and the fixed arm counts imply
\[
 \mathbb E\{(P-\overline T)W_n\mid z\}
 =-\mathbb E(W_n^2\mid z).                              \tag{24}
\]
Expanding around \(\mu\), using
\(\mathbb E[(\overline T-\mu)W_n]
 =\mathbb E[(\overline T-\mu)(\zeta_O-\mu)]\), and completing the posterior square gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E(H_n-\zeta_O)^2
 &=B_P(q)-\mathbb EW_n^2
   +2\mathbb E[(\overline T-\mu)(\zeta_O-\mu)]-D(q)\\
 &\geq B_P(q)-\mathbb EW_n^2-2\sqrt{S(q)D(q)}-D(q).
 \end{aligned}                                         \tag{25}
\]
Every term in (25) concerns the realized finite-population target.

Let \(a_n=n^{1/3}\) and
\(D_n(q)=L_n+J(q)H(q)/a_n\).  Equations (19)--(25) yield the explicit computable envelope
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
 \leq{}&a_n\left\{1-\frac{H(q)}{D_n(q)}\right\}
 +\overline V_{k,\varepsilon}\\
 &+2C_{k,\varepsilon}
 \left[
 \frac{H(q)\{D_n(q)-1\}}{D_n(q)}
 \right]^{1/2}
 +\frac{C_{k,\varepsilon}^2}{a_n}.
\end{aligned}                                          \tag{26}
\]

We now maximize this envelope without omitting allocation faces.  On the local set in the theorem statement, (11) gives
\(H(q)-1=O(n^{-11/36})\).  Equations (13)--(15) then give
\[
 \beta(q)^2+\gamma(q)^2=O(n^{-11/36}),
 \qquad J(q)=I_k+O_{k,\varepsilon}(n^{-11/36}).         \tag{27}
\]
Also \(a_n(L_n-1)=O_{k,\varepsilon}(n^{-1/3})\).  Substitution in (26) shows, uniformly on the local set,
\[
 G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
 \leq I_k+\overline V_{k,\varepsilon}+o_{k,\varepsilon}(1)
 =\mathcal E_{k,\varepsilon}+o_{k,\varepsilon}(1).    \tag{28}
\]
If the sharper local parameterization in (9) holds, (11) gives
\[
 a_n\{H(q)-1\}\longrightarrow
 2\sum_a\frac{u_a^2}{|c_a^\dagger|},                  \tag{29}
\]
while all other limits in (27)--(28) are unchanged.  Keeping the negative term in the first line of (26) proves (9).  This independently verifies that the local maximizer is \(q^\dagger\).

For completeness, consider the positive-count exterior.  Its definition and (11) imply
\[
 a_n\{H(q)-1\}\geq n^{1/36}.                          \tag{30}
\]
For fixed \((k,\varepsilon)\), the constants in (26) are finite.  If
\(H(q)\leq a_n/(2J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max})\), then
\(D_n(q)\leq2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  On \(1\leq H\leq2\), (30) inserted directly in (26) sends its right side to \(-\infty\).  On \(2\leq H\leq4\), one has \(D_n(q)-H\leq-1/4\) eventually, so the first term in (26) is at most \(-a_n/8\).  On \(4\leq H\leq a_n/(2J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max})\), one has \(D_n(q)-H\leq-H/4\), so that term is at most \(-a_nH/8\).  In both subranges the square-root term is
\(O_{k,\varepsilon}(\sqrt H+H/\sqrt{a_n})\), and is dominated by the displayed negative bound.  These are comparisons of explicit rational powers.

If \(H(q)>a_n/(2J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max})\), use (19) and the monotonicity of \(H/(L_n+J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max}H/a_n)\) to obtain
\[
 B_P(q)\geq\frac{a_n}{4J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max}n}     \tag{31}
\]
eventually.  The \(L^2\) triangle inequality between \(H_n\), \(P\), and an arbitrary data action, together with (23), gives
\[
 \{mathbb E(H_n-D)^2\}^{1/2}
 \geq \sqrt{B_P(q)}-sqrt{\mathbb EW_n^2}.
\]
Equations (23) and (31) imply a lower bound of order
\(n^{-2/3}/J_{k,\varepsilon}^{\max}\), which is strictly larger than \(n^{-1}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Thus the exterior maximum of \(G\) is eventually below the right side of (8).

Finally suppose at least one arm count is zero, and let \(F\) be the set of observed arms.  Choose a two-arm face containing \(F\), and use its direction in (2).  Its observed Bernoulli likelihood is constant along that direction by (6), its target derivative is one, and its product-prior directional information is a finite explicitly rationally bounded number \(J_F\).  The integration-by-parts argument (17), now with zero likelihood information, gives
\[
 B_P(q)\geq\alpha^2/J_F.                               \tag{32}
\]
Combining (32), (23), and the same \(L^2\) triangle inequality gives Bayes risk of order \(n^{-2/3}/J_F\), again strictly larger than \(n^{-1}\).  This proves the zero-face part.

All constants just used are obtained by rational matrix inversion, finite type and sign-cell enumeration, and exact integration of the verified rational splines and polynomial transverse density.  The inequalities after (26) involve only rational constants and ordered algebraic powers of \(n\).  Enumerating \(n\) until their monotone upper bounds are below \(\eta\) therefore terminates and returns \(N(k,\varepsilon,\eta)\).  Equations (28), (30)--(32) prove (8) with that effective threshold.  Finally, the effective Airy-record lemma gives
\[
 \frac{4\int| (\varphi_k^\dagger)'|^2
 +(5/8)\int|x|(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}
 {\int(\varphi_k^\dagger)^2}
 \leq\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+2^{-k},
\]
so sending \(k\to\infty\) and \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) in the local saddle yields \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\), as claimed.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(n,k\geq1\), rationals \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\), and a verified spline record.  If \(\alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\leq1\), finite-input mode of \(\mathsf E\) terminates and returns rational \(b^-\leq b^+\) with
\[
 b^-\leq B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\leq b^+,
 \qquad b^+-b^-\leq\delta,
 \qquad R_n(c^\dagger)\geq B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\geq b^-.
\]
It also returns exact ordered-field maxima of \(G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\) on the three allocation strata and an exact rational action-grid value \(U\) attained by a total procedure under \(q^\dagger\), with \(R_n(c^\dagger)\leq U\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex: The tangent lemma supplies positivity.  Every fiber probability is affine over each of finitely many rational spline and sign cells, so expansion of the multinomial probability and integration against the three rational piecewise-polynomial densities gives an element of \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\).  The response counts, allocation counts, observations, and factorial tables are finite.  Hence all posterior numerators, denominators, risks, and stratum maxima are computed by finitely many ordered-field operations.  Sturm isolation for the square-free polynomial \(nX^3-1\) decides signs and refines the final minimum to any requested rational width, proving termination and the first two inequalities.  The face-robust orbit lemma gives the inequality against \(R_n(c^\dagger)\).  The rational action-grid program is finite; a feasible optimizer defines a total randomized estimator, and its finitely many schedule risks verify \(R_n(c^\dagger)\leq U\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), there is one Turing machine extending \(\mathsf E\) with the following properties.  On input \(n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\), it outputs an index \(k_n\), the complete verified spline record for \(\varphi_{k_n}^\dagger\), a rational \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}>0\), rational nonnegative errors \(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), and \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), and finite ordered-field certificates.  The outputs satisfy
\[
 k_n\uparrow\infty,
 \qquad \varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\downarrow0,
 \qquad
 \alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+4\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})\leq1.
\]
For
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_n&=\left\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0,
\ \left\|n^{1/6}(r/n-q^\dagger)\right\|_\infty
\le n^{1/72}\right\},\\
\mathcal X_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0\}\setminus\mathcal L_n,\\
\mathcal Z_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a=0\},
\end{aligned}
\]
the certified all-count conclusions are
\[
\begin{aligned}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{loc},n}&& (r\in\mathcal L_n),\\
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)

proposed.comparator_claim: The unrestricted two-arm binary minimax risk equals \(n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) and is attained by Bernoulli randomization with nonlinear shrinkage.
For the two-arm bounded-outcome game, independent assignment remains minimax when estimators are unrestricted.
Under permutation-invariant law classes and linear estimation schemes, complete randomization with Neyman allocation is minimax.
A first-order local asymptotic minimax bound applies across broad sequential experimental designs, including multiple treatments.
Pairwise-independent inclusion attains the sharp bounded-total minimax risk within the class of unbiased estimators.
Limits of experiments yield asymptotically optimal treatment rules under average and minimax risk criteria in smooth models.
Second-order minimax optimality can be characterized through positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.

prose_updates.tldr: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the unrestricted outcome-independent design game and the fixed independent allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) have the same sharp second-order coefficient \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\).  The proof replaces the refuted scalar tube by a three-coordinate response-type prior.  Its common-shift coordinate gives exact guards for every single-arm and two-arm allocation face, a derived van Trees envelope controls all positive allocation counts, and the permutation-orbit argument covers arbitrary dependent labeled designs.  A terminating rational evaluator supplies finite lower and upper certificates and a computable tail majorant.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent supplied the first-order value, the second-order order, and finite response-type games, but no sharp all-design coefficient.  A scalar Airy path fails on a zero face because one arm reveals its longitudinal coordinate.  The missing mathematical object was a design-independent full-dimensional local prior together with a uniform finite-population Bayes transfer over local, exterior, and zero-count allocations.
project_justification.niche: At the unequal three-arm contrast, the zero-cost common-mean direction and the nonzero transverse direction jointly hide the target coordinate on every proper allocation face without changing the causal estimand.  This face geometry is absent from the two-arm Airy problem and is essential when designs may put zero probability on an arm.
project_justification.fill: The response alphabet is solved by explicit signed tangent measures.  The resulting compact rational three-coordinate prior has exact positivity and target moments.  A direction-wise van Trees inequality, an exact Horvitz--Thompson covariance identity, and the allocation identity \(H(q)-1=\sum_a(q_a-q_a^\dagger)^2/q_a\) yield a computable uniform Bayes envelope.  Diagonalizing verified rational Airy splines and transverse widths gives the sharp all-design limit, a total attaining procedure, and effective finite-to-limit certificates.

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including dependence across labeled units and zero allocation to an arm.  The face-robust prior is fixed independently of that design; conditioning on an allocation count and unit-permutation invariance reduce every design to the exact finite orbit likelihood without loss.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed.  Positive local counts, positive exterior counts, and zero-count faces are proved separately.  Exact face-guard directions make the target remain uncertain whenever any active arm is unobserved.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no superpopulation nuisance estimation.  Two compact prior coordinates lie in contrast-orthogonal directions: one changes the unequal-arm response geometry and one shifts all arm means together.  Their widths are held fixed in each uniform calculation and then decreased on a computably slow diagonal.

prose_updates.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) and Hull (2026) establish two-arm sharp minimax results.  The present result derives the unequal three-arm coefficient under the larger class of every outcome-independent dependent design.  Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) motivate limit-experiment and spectral methods, but the response-type positivity, realized finite-population target correction, allocation-face guards, exact orbit transfer, and computable uniform remainder are derived here.  Bai (2023), Armstrong (2022), and Aronow and Lopatto (2026) impose different estimator, law, or first-order restrictions.  Hammer et al. (1996) supplies only prospective complete binary-endpoint regimen-trial motivation; no censored-outcome reanalysis is claimed.
prose_updates.interpretation: For the fixed unequal three-regimen contrast, allowing dependent assignment or optimizing over all outcome-independent designs gives no second-order advantage over independent allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\).  A protocol designer can use the total Airy-feedback procedure and can request an exact finite-sample rational risk bracket plus a certified sample-size threshold for a desired second-order tolerance.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(K=3,n=3\) full-label risk \(511653/4000000\) lies below the scalar Bayes value \(18213/136000\), and the preserved scalar diagnostic explains why that path cannot prove the asymptotic theorem.  The successful prior adds a common-shift guard; its fixed-width face paths are load-bearing.  The theorem is pointwise in the fixed rational contrast and fixed arm count.  It does not provide a computationally uniform modulus as a contrast weight vanishes, and the evaluator's exhaustive finite alphabets are not claimed to run in polynomial time.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The unrestricted sharp equality, equality of the independent and unrestricted second-order values, and the cross-sample effective certificate are proved for \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) with fixed three-arm support and binary outcomes.  The response-cost program and fixed-independent theorem remain available for other fixed permitted contrasts, but no unrestricted sharp theorem is claimed there.  No growing-arm, uniform vanishing-weight, censored-endpoint, or arbitrary-real computability claim is made.  Real contrasts have an explicit mathematical response-cost approximation route, while certified execution requires a rational input representation.
